scope.note: This repository holds NO repository-level secrets. Every credential below is environment-scoped, which is why each new environment forces fresh hand-provisioning and why P-6 precondition reachability is the governing question for all of them. Measured 2026-08-07 with `gh secret list --repo rexcoleman/rexcoleman.dev` (empty) and `gh api repos/rexcoleman/rexcoleman.dev/environments`.

expiry.reason: A raw ed25519 private key carries no expiry of its own. Its AUTHORITY expires: each issued attestation has a 24-hour lifetime, and the key is only as current as the trust root pinned in the frozen bundle.

reestablishing_transition.detail: This key reached this environment by a manual out-of-band act. No registered transition re-establishes it. Rotating it would need FRESH key material, and Rex's binding ruling forbids any walkthrough that asks the owner to generate, paste, or hold a signing key value, so the correct fix is an in-platform key-generation-and-rotation transition that does not yet exist.

compensating_lapse_detection.how_it_detects: The key is exercised on every renewal. If it were lost or corrupted, the very next scheduled renewal fails at the signing step, at least 6 hours before the live 24-hour authority could expire. Detection therefore precedes outage rather than following it.
compensating_lapse_detection.residual_risk: Detection is not prevention. If the key is LOST there is no registered path to restore it; the system would fail closed and stay closed until the missing rotation transition is built.

expiry.reason: Same key material as the issuer-held copy; no credential-level expiry.

reestablishing_transition.invocation: gh workflow run provision-renewal-signing-key.yml --repo rexcoleman/rexcoleman.dev --ref main -f mode=copy
reestablishing_transition.detail: Reads the key from rea-write-enforcement-issuer and writes it to rea-write-enforcement-renewal through the GitHub secrets API public-key encryption path. Idempotent; verifies the target secret by name and refuses unless the observed updated_at proves THIS run wrote it.
owner_acts: approve the one rea-write-enforcement-issuer deployment this workflow requests

expiry.reason: Not yet minted. GitHub fixes a fine-grained PAT's expiry at mint time and the owner chooses it, so the real date IS knowable and MUST be written into this row at provisioning. Recording it is part of the provisioning step, not an afterthought.

lapse_detection.cadence: on demand, and as the first action of any mode=copy run
lapse_detection.how_it_detects: probe_write_scope() GETs the target environment's secrets public-key endpoint before writing anything. An expired or revoked PAT fails that probe and produces the typed refusal SECRETS_WRITE_PAT_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE naming the exact permission required, instead of a partial write.
lapse_detection.residual_risk: The probe fires only when the workflow is invoked. A PAT that lapses between invocations is discovered at the next invocation, which is acceptable because nothing depends on the PAT between invocations.

reestablishing_transition.sanctioned_by: Rex ruling 2026-08-07 (Option A, binding): the owner's only acts are to mint a PAT and to approve one issuance.
owner_acts: mint a fine-grained PAT scoped to repository rexcoleman/rexcoleman.dev only, permission Secrets: Read and write
store it as environment secret REA_SECRETS_WRITE_PAT in rea-write-enforcement-issuer
record its expiry date in this file
reestablishing_transition.detail: This is the bootstrap root of the custody chain. It is a manual act by construction: a token that lets automation write secrets cannot itself be established by automation that has no secrets. It is recorded as a sanctioned owner act rather than hidden, and it never involves key material -- the owner mints a token, never a signing key.

expiry.reason: GitHub App private keys do not expire. They are valid until explicitly revoked in the App's settings.

reestablishing_transition.detail: Re-establishment requires generating a new private key in the GitHub App settings UI and hand-provisioning it. No registered transition exists, and none can read the key out of App settings, so this is structurally the same class of gap as the issuer signing key.

compensating_lapse_detection.cadence: every independent second-principal review, i.e. every capability_change issuance
compensating_lapse_detection.how_it_detects: The key is consumed by actions/create-github-app-token at the start of the review job. A revoked key fails token minting immediately and blocks the review rather than producing an unattested pass.
compensating_lapse_detection.residual_risk: Only exercised on capability_change issuances, so a revocation could sit undetected between them. It cannot cause a silent WRONG result -- it fails closed -- but it can surface late.

expiry.reason: `gh secret list` and GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/environments/{env}/secrets return created_at and updated_at ONLY. GitHub exposes no expiry field for a secret's CONTENTS, and the contents are write-only, so no automated path in this repository can read or derive this token's expiry. The date is not being withheld; it is genuinely unavailable. Do not fabricate one.

lapse_detection.detector: .github/workflows/renew-write-enforcement-attestation.yml -> issue-write-enforcement-attestation.yml job renew-wea, step 'Checkout frozen repositories'
lapse_detection.how_it_detects: This is the structural compensation for an unreadable expiry. The token is exercised by checkout_manifest.py on every renewal attempt. A lapsed token fails that step, and because renewal runs 4 times inside each 24-hour authority lifetime, the failure is observed at least 6 hours BEFORE the live attestation expires. Lapse therefore surfaces as a failed run while enforcement is still valid, which is exactly the window in which it can be fixed without an outage. Silent lapse -- the failure mode that already cost this cycle an outage -- is what this structure removes.
lapse_detection.residual_risk: Surfacing depends on someone seeing the failed run. The run failure itself is deterministic and unmissable in the Actions list, but proactive alerting on it has NOT been independently verified and is a separate open item.

reestablishing_transition.invocation: issue-write-enforcement-attestation.yml job issue-wea step Validate protected bundle token and provision downstream CI
owner_acts: approve the exact rea-write-enforcement-issuer deployment
reestablishing_transition.detail: Inside the protected issuer job, the transition validates the existing bundle token with exact Git reads across all five frozen repositories and the exact predecessor Actions artifact before any downstream mutation. It then uses the separately scoped REA_SECRETS_WRITE_PAT only for the downstream secret write and exact post-name/update verification. Neither credential is exposed to the owner arc or output.

expiry.reason: Same as REA_BUNDLE_READ_TOKEN: the GitHub secrets API exposes created_at and updated_at only, never an expiry for the secret's contents.

lapse_detection.how_it_detects: The token is exercised by `gh api repos/rexcoleman/newsletter/rulesets/19564990` on every renewal attempt, and the following step refuses a ruleset response that does not normalize. A lapsed token fails at least 6 hours before the live authority expires.
lapse_detection.residual_risk: Same as REA_BUNDLE_READ_TOKEN: detection is deterministic, proactive alerting is unverified.

reestablishing_transition.sanctioned_by: Rex ruling 2026-08-07 (Option A, binding): minting a token is a sanctioned owner act.

store it as environment secret REA_RULESET_READ_TOKEN in rea-write-enforcement-issuer
record the mint date and chosen expiry in this file

expiry.reason: Measured 2026-09-07: `gh secret list --repo rexcoleman/rexcoleman.dev` returns nothing and GET /repos/rexcoleman/rexcoleman.dev/environments/rea-write-enforcement-issuer/secrets does not list this name, so the credential is not provisioned anywhere yet. Once it is: a GitHub App's numeric ID and its private key do not expire, which is the whole point of this route -- the installation TOKEN minted from them lives about an hour and is never stored. Do not record an expiry for either name; there is none to record.

lapse_detection.detector: .github/write-enforcement/select_governed_read_credential.py, run as step 'Select the governed read credential under custody precedence' in every issuance, renewal and external-judge run, and owner_rails/kc80_github_app/app_rail.sh on gios-dev
lapse_detection.cadence: cron 17 */6 * * * for the renewal path (4 attempts per 24-hour authority lifetime); on dispatch for the others
lapse_detection.how_it_detects: The selector prints the route it chose on every run. route=github_app_installation_token means the App pair was complete and one short-lived installation token was minted and verified against all five repositories. A PARTIAL pair fails the run loudly with GOVERNED_READ_APP_PAIR_PARTIAL rather than downgrading, so a half-provisioned or half-rotated App cannot be mistaken for a working one. The App private key does not expire, so the failure mode this detects is misprovisioning rather than lapse.
lapse_detection.residual_risk: A WHOLLY ABSENT App pair is NOT a failure: custody requires the deprecated REA_BUNDLE_READ_TOKEN fallback in that case, so the run prints route=deprecated_compatibility_rea_bundle_read_token and succeeds. Absence is therefore observable in the run log but does not stop a run. That is the state TODAY -- neither name is set in any scope -- so the expiring compatibility token is still what the freeze depends on until the App is created.

reestablishing_transition.sanctioned_by: CREDENTIAL_CUSTODY.md section 'Primary GitHub App custody for governed-project reads': the owner creates and installs the App through GitHub's App settings. GitHub exposes no API that creates a GitHub App or generates its private key, so no automated transition can exist for this credential; the owner act is irreducible rather than a convenience.
owner_acts: create a GitHub App owned by rexcoleman with Contents: Read-only and no other permission
install it on the rexcoleman account limited to exactly govML, research_enforcement_activation, Moonshots_Career_Thesis, newsletter and rexcoleman.dev
generate its private key and run owner_rails/kc80_github_app/app_rail.sh <APP_ID> <pem> on gios-dev, which installs both names into ~/.config/govml/env append-and-preserve
reconcile the two names into this repository as secrets so hosted runs can read them
reestablishing_transition.detail: The private key never passes through a log, an argument, or this record. The rail base64-encodes it in place, writes atomically at mode 0600, preserves every unrelated name in the env file byte for byte, and prints presence only. github_app_installation_token.py then proves installation identity, Contents:Read-only permission and the exact five-repository set before it mints anything.

lapse_detection.detector: .github/write-enforcement/setup_external_judge_hosted_principal.py --preflight, and at use time .github/workflows/issue-external-judge-authority.yml job issue, step 'Approve exact request with protected hosted principal'
lapse_detection.cadence: on demand for --preflight; on workflow_dispatch for the consuming step, which has no schedule and has run exactly once (rexcoleman.dev run 33394886672, 2026-08-31, failed)
lapse_detection.how_it_detects: The setup tool's --preflight reads the live remote state and reports READY_FOR_ONE_TIME_SETUP or an idempotent COMPLETE, so absence and partial provisioning are both observable without mutating anything. At use time the workflow asserts the secret is non-empty before invoking the checked-out govML issuer, so an unprovisioned or emptied principal fails the run rather than producing an unsigned authority.
lapse_detection.residual_risk: Neither surface runs on a schedule, so absence surfaces when someone looks or when someone dispatches. The one rexcoleman.dev run to date never reached the consuming step: it failed earlier at the cross-repository govML checkout, which s210 repaired by minting through the governed selector.

reestablishing_transition.sanctioned_by: The registered signed-release adapter research-enforcement-activation-generation-5-s169-hosted-principal-v1, described in SIGNED_RELEASE_CONVERGENCE_INDEX.md as binding 'the one-time checked owner setup with tested rollback'. Every registered adapter additionally declares boundaries.owner_rail = irreducible-human-only. The one-time GitHub authentication that establishes a protected environment and its fixed root-owned public half is an owner-held capability with no automated substitute; EXTERNAL_JUDGE_HOSTED_PRINCIPAL.md states this in its Status and boundary section.
reestablishing_transition.invocation: bash .github/write-enforcement/setup_external_judge_hosted_principal.sh (execs /usr/bin/python3 .github/write-enforcement/setup_external_judge_hosted_principal.py --apply after proving hostname, uid, and a clean byte-for-byte checkout of the exact protected origin/main payload)
owner_acts: authenticate gh once as rexcoleman with the scope needed to create a protected environment
run the registered one-time row, which execs setup_external_judge_hosted_principal.py --apply

the tool then creates environment govml-external-judge-approver in rexcoleman/govML with the exact deployment-branch policy (PUT /repos/rexcoleman/govML/environments/govml-external-judge-approver, then POST .../deployment-branch-policies)

it sets the three environment variables GOVML_EXTERNAL_JUDGE_APPROVING_PUBLIC_KEY_SHA256, GOVML_EXTERNAL_JUDGE_ISSUER_COMMIT and GOVML_EXTERNAL_JUDGE_ISSUER_SHA256, re-reading remote state after each one and refusing PARTIAL_ENVIRONMENT_DRIFT_REFUSED on any divergence
it sets the environment secret GOVML_EXTERNAL_JUDGE_APPROVING_PRIVATE_KEY_PEM by piping the private half to `gh secret set`, so the value never enters argv, a log, or this record
it marks GOVML_EXTERNAL_JUDGE_SETUP_STATE = complete:<public_key_sha256> only after the full postmark state matches
on any failure after the environment is created it deletes the partial environment and verifies absence, which is the tested rollback the adapter binds
reestablishing_transition.detail: This row's credential_id names the rexcoleman.dev consumption site, but the sanctioned act provisions rexcoleman/govML, because that is where the REGISTERED consumer lives. govML's own copy of the workflow checks itself out ('Checkout the exact govML workflow commit', no repository input) and asserts GITHUB_REPOSITORY == rexcoleman/govML, so it never needed a cross-repository token; only the rexcoleman.dev copy did. The rexcoleman.dev copy is nevertheless the one that is a signed member (hosted-external-judge-authority-workflow, commit 1ba570ccd37cd032e77b3e102903f9518d63590a), which is why it reads as authoritative. Running the sanctioned setup will NOT populate this locus, and populating this locus would not make the registered client dispatch it: the client's html_url check refuses anything but govML. The duplicate's disposition -- retire the rexcoleman.dev copy, or register it -- is a signed-population change reserved to the kernel coach and is tracked as govml_hardening_queue row 146. Recorded here so the next reader is not misled into provisioning the wrong repository.
